answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a real cost for reputation: each agent must stake tokens and build a verifiable history of useful work before it earns voting weight or rewards. A fresh identity starts at its nadir, with no trust, while a proven agent that has climbed toward the summit of reliability keeps its standing only by continuing honest work. Cheap copies crumble like shale under that cost, because spawning a thousand new identities buys no history, no stake, and no trust.
